page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.large is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core via hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 8.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware capabilities include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets, supported by a 33 MB L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network interface without GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results place the instance within entry-level tiers for computational throughput. In CPU tests, the system achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 1114.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 1822.26, reflecting the throughput limits of a single physical core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 10.25 GB/sec for large uncached read operations and 9.61 GB/sec for write operations. Application-level benchmarks show 1.53 million operations per second in Redis SET tasks and a static web serving rate of 1.31 GB/sec.

Because the server relies entirely on external network storage and shares a single physical CPU core across both vCPUs, resource-heavy parallel tasks and high-throughput I/O pipelines will face clear hardware bottlenecks. The instance is best matched to entry-level production deployments, staging environments, internal microservices, and lightweight web serving where memory-to-core balance is prioritized over raw compute power.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.large is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed under the KVM hypervisor, it features 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes AVX-512 and AES instruction sets but does not incorporate bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits entry-level performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1114.0, uncached memory read bandwidth of 10.25 GB/sec, and Redis throughput of 1.53 million operations per second. While throughput is constrained under compute-heavy scenarios due to the dual-thread single-core topology, the balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio provides steady resources for low-volume web serving, staging workloads, small microservices, and lightweight administrative tasks.
